description:
Redwood Inference’s Optimize product can apply cost-saving configuration changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles, routing tweaks) that materially impact response quality. This project introduces mandatory quality guardrails that gate any Optimize-driven config application behind evaluation checks and regression thresholds.

Goals:
- Prevent user-visible quality regressions when applying cost optimizations.
- Standardize how prompt sets, eval suites, and thresholds are defined, stored, and audited.
- Make gating outcomes actionable: clear pass/fail reasons, rollback hooks, and monitoring/alerts.
- Provide a safe rollout path: feature flags, canaries, and gradual enforcement.

Scope:
- “Gating” is enforced at the control-plane layer where Optimize proposals are applied (UI and API).
- Integrate with eval-harness and prompt-set libraries to run targeted eval suites per model/workload.
- Define a threshold schema (per metric, per model family, per workload type) including statistical rules and minimum sample sizes.
- Add telemetry + dashboards that correlate config changes to quality and cost outcomes.
- Add operational runbooks for failures, overrides, and incident handling.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the eval-harness; the project extends and standardizes it.
- Fully automated model selection or customer-specific bespoke eval authoring (supported, but not built as a services engagement).

Key stakeholders:
- Product (Optimize): Aditya Rao (DRI), coordinates requirements, UX expectations, and rollout policy.
- Applied ML / Evals: Jonas Weber, Selene Huang, Sana Farid, Karthik Iyer (threshold methodology, eval suites, statistical guardrails).
- Platform Control Plane / Policy Engine: Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee (enforcement point, config schema, policy evaluation, auditability).
- Serving Runtime & Performance: Mateo Alvarez, Sofia Ivanova, Noah Patel (runtime-level constraints, perf suite alignment, “safe” batching/caching behaviors).
- SRE: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton (rollout, monitoring, paging criteria, incident playbooks).
- Telemetry/Analytics: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman (metrics, data quality, reporting).

Timeline (plausible):
- Phase 0 (Discovery, 2–3 weeks): define metrics, prompt set coverage targets, initial thresholds, and enforcement design.
- Phase 1 (Build, 4–6 weeks): threshold schema + policy engine integration + eval runner + UI/API gating plumbing.
- Phase 2 (Pilot, 3–4 weeks): internal canary + a small set of design partners; iterate on false positives/negatives.
- Phase 3 (GA, 2–4 weeks): default-on gating for Optimize config changes; controlled override path with auditing.

Deliverables:
- Confluence: PRD, design/ADR set, threshold spec, operational runbooks, and standards updates.
- Linear: project/initiative and execution tickets.
- GitHub: PRs implementing schema, gate checks, eval-harness integration, dashboards, and docs.
- Slack: coordination threads, decision-making, rollout comms, and triage.
- Drive: working drafts, spreadsheets for threshold tuning, launch checklist.
- Support artifacts (Jira/Gmail/Fireflies/HubSpot): a few customer-driven incidents/escalations that motivate and validate the feature.

Definition of supported quality metrics (task success, rubric scores, toxicity, factuality proxies), normalization rules, and how thresholds are expressed per workload/model family.
Plan for prompt set coverage: required scenarios by product surface (chat, tool-calling, structured output), sampling strategy, and ownership for ongoing maintenance.
Design for invoking eval-harness from Optimize apply: inputs/outputs, caching of results, retries, and performance considerations.
Triage workflow when gating fails: how to identify metric regressions vs noise, when to adjust thresholds, and when to block a rollout.
Guardrails specific to quantization profiles: allowed transitions, per-model exclusions, minimum eval suites, and known failure modes (formatting drift, reasoning degradation).
ADR choosing the enforcement layer (control plane vs runtime vs console): tradeoffs, auditability, failure handling, and backward compatibility.
ADR for threshold config schema, versioning strategy, and how thresholds are pinned to model versions and prompt-set revisions.

Operational runbook: diagnosing gating outages/timeouts, safe-degrade behavior, override procedure, and rollback steps.
Dashboard definitions: gating pass rate, failure reasons, eval latency, override usage, and correlation with post-change customer quality signals.
Matrix tying perf suite scenarios to quality checks: which optimizations require which evals, plus guidance for mixed prompt-length workloads.

Internal outline for customer-facing docs: how guardrails work, what metrics are used, how customers supply prompt sets, and what ‘failed gating’ means.

Spreadsheet-style doc: KPIs (quality regressions prevented, cost savings preserved), definitions, data sources, and targets per quarter.

Working gap analysis: which customer workloads are underrepresented in prompt sets; proposed additions and owners.

Notes on telemetry design: metric names, labels, cardinality risks, and sampling strategy for eval results.
